slides.title: Day 1 late: a friendly reminder
slides.text: Assume they forgot. Keep it light.
slides.box: Hi Sam, quick reminder that invoice #104 was due yesterday. I've attached it again here. Thanks so much!
slides.label: Copy this

slides.title: Day 7: a second reminder
slides.text: Ask if something is blocking it.
slides.box: Hi Sam, following up on invoice #104, now a week overdue. Is anything holding it up on your side? Happy to help.
slides.label: Copy this

slides.title: Day 21: a final notice
slides.text: Calm, clear, with one date.
slides.box: Hi Sam, invoice #104 is now 3 weeks overdue. Please pay it by this Friday. After that I'll need to pause work on the project.
slides.label: Copy this

slides.title: Write down every reminder
slides.text: Note the day you sent each one. Then you know when to send the next, and you never send two in one day.

carousels.caption:

Day 1 late: a friendly reminder

Day 21: a final notice with one clear date

slides.title:
5 questions
before you
quote
slides.sub: so the price is right the first time

slides.title: What does "done" look like?
slides.text: Get the finish line in writing. It stops "one more thing" later.

slides.title: What's the deadline?
slides.text: Rush work takes more of your time. It's fair to charge more for it.

slides.title: How many feedback rounds?
slides.text: Agree on a number. Unlimited changes means unlimited work.

slides.title: What's the budget range?
slides.text: It saves you both from a proposal that was never going to fit.

slides.title: Who approves the work?
slides.text: One decision maker means fewer surprises at the end.

carousels.caption:
